system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 1, and the digit 7 as a null.
system.notes: Lasry's filed key (ASV - S423) values only the two-digit elements; none of the 166 four-digit groups in the corpus (708 tokens). The nomenclator is not alphabetical as far as the recovered values show.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's reconstructed key ASV - S423 and segmented decipherment of Spagna 423/1-11, attached to every one of DECODE R179-R188; key dated 24 October 2020

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE session cookie; set the target by /goal.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R179-R188 record pages and all attachments (per-item transcriptions, key, corpus decipherment, page images).
Checked attachments first, following the Spagna 364D precedent: Lasry's key ASV - S423 (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of all 11 items are on every record.
Parsed the aligned decipherment (9,001 tokens incl. nulls): the key values no four-digit group; 166 distinct groups, 708 tokens, unread. Text read 90.6%.
Tried the 364D alphabetical-bracket method; the 1736 nomenclator is not alphabetical (1222 -mente, 1245 -zione, 1882 Spagna, 1935 V.S.), so values must come from context alone.
Assigned 46 groups from context, accepting a value only where every occurrence reads (N.S., V.S., S. Sede, Corte, Spagna, Napoli, Brevi, Sig. Card., -mente, -zione, tutt-, molt-, altr- ...).
Re-measured: 424 of 708 nomenclator tokens valued; whole text 90.6% -> 95.3% read. Content consistent with the 1736 Spanish recruiting riots in Rome (Acquaviva, Montemar, Molina).

Catalogue entry 250 (DECODE R26, 7 Jan 1736) identified as item 423/1 of this volume, filed apart from R179-R188; already covered by Lasry's decipherment and reading.txt. Entry closed, no new reading.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per item, the digit stream (lasry/423-*.txt) and, for items 2-11, the DECODE transcription (decode/keep/DOC_R*.txt); the decryption is reading.txt (Lasry's decipherment with the nomenclator values recovered here), split per item into texts/reading_423-*.txt, plus Lasry's 2020 decipherment of the whole corpus; key: Lasry's filed key and key_extra.txt

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): the eleven running texts read through. Open nomenclator groups (about one per eight to ten words) and ??? runs stand in almost every sentence of ten letters, relabelled decoded, not read; the short 423/3 builds its sentence (reviewed B). Class already solved -> read in part; fraction_read 0.953 (tokens valued) -> 0.016.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b04): the 26 DECODE page images of R26 and R179-R188 fetched with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/b04_fetch.py; scratchpad only, not in the repository) and R26's transcription DOC_R26_D1635 (NiLan 2017) saved to decode/keep/. The pages carry no interlinear or margin decipherment; the clear text in the margins of some images is the facing leaf of other letters. A web search found no edition of the 1736 ciphers to Guiccioli; the minutes would be in the Madrid nunciature archive (not digitised).

The DECODE transcriptions re-segmented with Lasry's rules (7 null outside groups, 1xxx nomenclator, else pairs; b04_seg.py) instead of Lasry's segmented file, which leaves out whole runs (423/5: 137 of 177 non-null tokens; about 20% in all). Fifteen unclear or struck figures resolved on the images and by sense (texts/423_b04_corrections.tsv); per-letter decodes in texts/423-<n>_decode_b04.txt.

Key corrected and extended from the documents (texts/b04_key_additions.txt): two-digit 25 = che (Lasry ";"), 30 = ta (not to), 69 = z (not t), 93 = nel (not quel); nomenclator 1234 = qual (was Ministr/Nunzi), 1205 = com (was che), 1241 = tant (was molt), 1210 = esser (was restar), each tested on every occurrence; 34 new firm values (medesim, cont, aver, fatt, Mons., ben, letter, part, issim, interess, relazion, pubblic, spagnuol, dett, parlar, Regn, volt, tre, due, ordinari, riguard, tropp, ragion, present, qualch, manier, liber, aggrav, ordin, avvis, procur, scriv, molt, Nunzi) and about 30 probable ones printed [?x].

Readings built sentence by sentence for 423/2, 423/4-11 (texts/423-<n>_reading.md, English _en.md) and aligned word by word with the decode (b04_align.py): every unbracketed word is carried by figures or a nomenclator value; supplied words bracketed. _check_reading.py on the bodies (abbreviations de-dotted): clean-sentence share 0.47-0.71 (the strict count treats every [?x] probable value as a hole).

423/1 (R26, 14 July 1736) read through on NiLan's weaker transcription (texts/423-1_reading.md, _en.md): the sentences of the riots, the Ostia and Trastevere enlistments, Acquaviva and Montemar build, but about a dozen runs do not decode (clean share 0.31); not re-transcribed from the images in this session.

Opened every attachment of DECODE R26 and R179-R188 at full resolution with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/r2d_fetch_docs.py): the png documents labelled 'cleartext' are not the cipher pages but neighbouring folios, and among them are contemporary clear copies ('Copia') of the ciphered letters 423/1 (ff. 284r-286r), 423/4 (f. 301r), 423/5 (f. 375r), 423/6 (f. 386r), 423/9 (ff. 416r-v), 423/10 (ff. 493r-494r) and 423/11 (ff. 509r-v). The 22 Oct re-read had opened only the IMG page images.

Transcribed the copies of 423/1, 5, 9, 11 (texts/423-<n>_copy.txt) and aligned each token by token with the re-segmented decode (research/reading_audit/r2d_align.py, texts/423-<n>_r2d_align.tsv); six figures of NiLan's R26 transcription corrected on the cipher images where the copy disagreed (texts/423_b04_corrections.tsv, item 1); 423/9 'io te danno', 423/11 'le la mede' and 'ben ..giata' found to be cipherer's slips on the images.

Key corrected and extended from the copies, each value checked at every occurrence (texts/b04_key_additions.txt, r2d block; research/reading_audit/r2d_kwic.py): 26 = del (not a) and 80 = dal (not nel); twelve earlier nomenclator values replaced (1219 ora, 1239 quell, 1608 necessari, 1229 perche, 1231 pero, 1818 ragguagli, 1699 pregiudizi, 1865 sodisfazion, 1218 avut, 1223 mentre, 1260 Ambasciator, 1368 congiuntur); about 55 groups valued (1513 Governator, 1544 Inquisitor, 1449 ecclesiastic, 1389 costi, day groups 1952 = 7, 1953 = 8, 1957 = 12, 1964 = 19 ...). Open groups: about 60 distinct on 22 Oct -> 12 now (12 distinct: three in 423/1, carried by the copy; four in 423/2, four in 423/7, one in 423/8).

423/1, 5, 9, 11 read from the copies and the figures (texts/423-<n>_reading.md, _en.md): v2 scores plain/explicit 423/1 0.41 -> 0.92/1.0, 423/5 0.60 -> 1.0/1.0, 423/9 0.72 -> 0.94/1.0, 423/11 0.56 -> 0.94/1.0 (body scored by research/reading_audit/r2d_score.py). The corrected key carried into the readings of 423/2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10 (research/reading_audit/r2d_fix_read.py, r2d_fix_read_en.py).

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): '## Reading' headings added to texts/423-2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 10_reading.md (bodies plain 0.619-1.0); texts/423-3_reading.md written from the b04 decode (plain 0.667, explicit 1.0). Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 11 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

texts.label: Spagna 423/1 (DECODE R26)
texts.summary: Clement XII's Secretariat of State to the nunciature in Madrid (Abbé Guiccioli) during the 1736 rupture with Spain: Spanish recruiting officers in Rome and the Papal State set off riots in Trastevere and at Velletri; the letters cover the tumults against the Holy See, Cardinal Acquaviva, the Duke of Montemar and Bishop Molina, and from October the padronato reale, the Regalist doctrines of the Madrid junta and the nomination of cardinals.

reading_review.note: Rome, 14 July 1736. Molina joins in the riots against the Holy See and puts forward the Donghi affair; the Emperor's demands after the Donghi affair were modest; Madrid, shown every indulgence over the Naples settlement, now claims things unconnected with the riots; the enlistments were forbidden, the Neapolitan officers and Acquaviva's rebuke known to all; Montemar stopped the same practice in Florence at once. Rests on the contemporary clear copy of the letter (ff. 284r-286r, DECODE R26 DOC_D963-D967, texts/423-1_copy.txt), found 23 Oct 2026 among the record's 'cleartext' png attachments, aligned token by token with the decode (texts/423-1_r2d_align.tsv) and checked on the cipher images where they disagree; the key corrected and extended from the copies (texts/b04_key_additions.txt, r2d block). Reading body: v2 score plain 0.922, explicit holes 1.0 (research/reading_audit/r2d_score.py). Look-alike alternates: none relied on; the copy confirms the text.
